blogs.title: Goodbye Tokens: How Byte‑Level Models are Changing the LLM Landscape
blogs.description: An introductory post that explains why traditional tokenizers are a bottleneck for large language models—covering issues like vocabulary bias, multilingual inequity, and fragility to noise—and how the Byte Latent Transformer (BLT) eliminates the need for a fixed vocabulary by operating directly on raw bytes.

blogs.title: From Bytes to Patches: The Secret Sauce Behind BLT’s Efficiency
blogs.description: A deep‑dive into BLT’s dynamic patching strategy. We break down static strided patches, whitespace‑based patches, and the novel entropy‑based patching that uses a tiny byte‑level model to decide where to split data, showing why adaptive patch sizes let BLT allocate compute where it matters most.

blogs.title: Inside BLT: The Three‑Part Architecture That Marries Local and Global Reasoning
blogs.description: An accessible walkthrough of BLT’s three components—a lightweight local encoder, a powerful global latent transformer, and a local decoder—illustrating how cross‑attention pools byte information into patches and then expands them back into text, and why this design beats token‑based transformers on both speed and flexibility.

blogs.title: Scaling Up Without Slowing Down: BLT’s FLOP‑Controlled Performance Gains
blogs.description: Explains the rigorous scaling experiments that show BLT matching Llama 3’s quality at up to 8 B parameters while using up to 50 % fewer inference FLOPs. The post translates technical scaling curves into plain English and highlights the practical benefits of growing both model size and patch size under a fixed compute budget.

blogs.title: Robustness by Design: How Byte‑Level Modeling Handles Noise, Characters, and Low‑Resource Languages
blogs.description: Shows how BLT’s direct access to bytes improves resistance to misspellings, random character drops, and other noise, plus its superior performance on character‑level benchmarks like CUTE, grapheme‑to‑phoneme tasks, and multilingual translation of long‑tail languages.

blogs.title: From Tokenizers to Bytes: Turning Existing LLMs into BLTs (and What Lies Ahead)
blogs.description: Discusses practical pathways for adopting BLT in production—distilling pre‑trained tokenized models into byte‑latent ones—and outlines future research directions such as end‑to‑end learned patching, wall‑clock speed optimizations, and extending scaling laws uniquely for byte‑level architectures.
